item.title: hp-Adaptive Finite Element Modeling of Static Cracks in Density-Dependent Media
item.description: arXiv:2611.33220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The elastostatic crack-tip fields within a density-dependent continuum are numerically investigated under several macroscopic loading configurations. The governing nonlinear boundary value problem is formulated using an algebraically nonlinear hyperelastic constitutive relationship in which the material moduli are intrinsically coupled to volumetric strain. Existence and uniqueness of the weak solution to the nonlinear displacement-based variational formulation are rigorously established at the continuous level via the Minty-Browder theorem. The variational formulation is then linearized at the partial differential equation level to construct a continuous damped Newton-Raphson scheme. To accurately capture the severe field gradients and internal singularities inherent to this model, the resulting sequence of linear operator equations is discretized and solved via a conforming finite element method within an $hp$-adaptive framework. A comparative analysis is conducted across five distinct boundary loading profiles (encompassing uniform, piecewise-slope, and concentrated point loads) applied to a stationary cracked geometry. Within each configuration, the density-dependent constitutive parameter is systematically varied to assess its regulatory impact on the fracture process zone, focusing on the spatial evolution of normal stress, normal strain, and strain energy density near the crack tip. Numerical results demonstrate that local kinematic deformability is strictly bounded by the strain-limiting nature of the continuum, whereby static equilibrium is sustained through severe, localized stress amplifications. Furthermore, the mechanical influence of the modeling parameter is fundamentally dictated by the topological interplay between internal crack geometry and the spatial distribution of applied macroscopic loads.
item.dc:creator: Vicente Valle Martinez, Saugata Ghosh, S. M. Mallikarjunaiah, Dambaru Bhatta

item.title: Error estimates for a structure-preserving finite-element scheme of quasi-incompressible Navier-Stokes-Maxwell-Stefan systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.33347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A conforming finite-element scheme for quasi-incompressible Navier-Stokes-Maxwell-Stefan systems in a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions is presented. The system consists of the Navier-Stokes equations, together with a quasi-incompressibility constraint, coupled with the cross-diffusion Maxwell--Stefan equations. The numerical scheme preserves the partial masses and the quasi-incompressibility constraint and dissipates the discrete energy. First-order error estimates in space and time are shown for a diffusion-augmented mobility matrix by using the relative energy method and suitable projection error estimates. Numerical experiments in two space dimensions illustrate the convergence of the scheme and indicate second-order convergence in space in the $L^2$ norm.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Brunk, Ansgar J\"ungel, Maria Luk\'a\v{c}ov\'a-Medvid'ov\'a

item.title: Adaptive Blockwise Tensor Trains for Stochastic Finite-Volume Methods with Uncertain Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.33529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic finite-volume (SFV) methods extend conservative, shock-capturing discretizations to hyperbolic systems with uncertain inputs by partitioning the parameter domain into finite-volume cells. However, their memory and computational cost grow exponentially with the number of uncertain parameters. Tensor-train (TT) formats can remove this exponential dependence, provided the ranks of the discrete solution remain small throughout the simulation. This requirement is frequently violated when the uncertainty is geometric. Mapping each realization onto a common reference domain introduces parameter-dependent metric factors, so that shocks and contacts propagate at different reference speeds and come to occupy different cells across realizations. The resulting rank growth is spatially localized - a structure that neither a single global TT nor a separate TT for each physical cell is able to exploit. We propose an adaptive blockwise TT representation in which the SFV solution is partitioned along its physical mode into contiguous blocks, each stored as an independent TT for every conserved variable. Blocks are split near discontinuities and in regions of large variance or rank, and merged where the solution is smooth. The mesh itself is never changed; only the grouping of cells into trains adapts. We embed this representation in a TT-based SFV solver combining WENO3 reconstruction in the physical and stochastic directions, positivity-preserving limiters, and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta time integration, with nonlinear steps evaluated via cross approximation. A mean-conservative rounding that adds no rank, together with single-valued interface fluxes, conserves the parameter-mean mass and energy to round-off for any partition. The approach is demonstrated on a Sod shock-tube problem with uncertain wall positions.
item.dc:creator: William P. Gammel, Steven T. Walton, Stephen A. Andrews, Svetlana Tokareva, William T. Taitano

item.title: FokasNets: Completing missing boundary data in Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Operators via the Global Relation
item.description: arXiv:2611.33549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce FokasNets, a framework that combines Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and operators (PINOs) with the Global Relation (GR) formulation of the Fokas method (also referred to as the Unified Transform), for mixed boundary problems. The general framework considers lifted representations of the neural network models, where the Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed by construction and the neural network learns the interior correction. The Global Relation is used as an additional solve during training that provides the missing boundary conditions to the lifted neural network, making training more efficient and accurate in the interior and on the boundary. We develop the construction of FokasNets for elliptic and evolution PDEs (Fokas-PINNs), and the corresponding PDE solution operator problems (Fokas Operator Networks - FONets), using the Global Relation formulations for these PDE classes. Furthermore, we develop the necessary theoretical framework for FokasNets, including error and stability analysis and show that FokasNets are universal approximators. We provide comprehensive numerical experiments, using examples with manufactured solutions and literature benchmarks. Compared to standard PINNs and Physics-Informed DeepONets and their lifted versions, FokasNets achieve significant improvements in solution accuracy in the interior and boundaries, both for single PDEs and particularly for solution operators, where the improvement reaches multiple orders of magnitude and fixed threshold errors are reached faster during training.
item.dc:creator: Kyriakos C. Georgiou, Khemraj Shukla, Athanassios S. Fokas, George Em Karniadakis

item.title: PACL: Patch-based Admissibility and Conservative Limiting framework for bound-preserving compact single-step DG methods for hyperbolic conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2611.33574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a Patch-based Admissibility and Conservative Limiting (PACL) framework for compact single-step discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations of hyperbolic conservation laws. The key idea is to establish admissibility of weighted averages over overlapping cell patches after a complete high-order time step. Continuous patch weights cancel interior numerical flux contributions, yielding admissibility estimates for weighted patch averages under suitable time-step conditions. A conservative patch correction uses these averages as reference states to obtain admissible physical cell averages, and a subsequent cellwise scaling enforces whole-cell or nodal admissibility in the original DG space. The framework requires neither a strong-stability-preserving decomposition nor auxiliary first-order discretizations, and all limiting is performed at the end of each time step. For scalar conservation laws, we prove a patchwise weak maximum principle for compact Runge--Kutta DG (cRKDG), ADER-DG with converged or fixed-Picard predictors, and Lax--Wendroff DG. We also prove that, under the stated local mesh and scaling assumptions, a single application of the scalar limiter preserves approximation order at active bounds, including flat extrema. For the compressible Euler equations, we establish patch admissibility for cRKDG and fixed-Picard ADER-DG under time-step conditions that maintain positive predictor density while allowing nonpositive predictor pressure. The analysis covers both exact spatial integration and compatible quadrature. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy and bound preservation, including problems with near-vacuum states and strong shocks.
item.dc:creator: Yue Wu, Zheng Sun

item.title: Anderson-Accelerated Landweber Iteration with Regularization Guarantees for Nonlinear Ill-Posed Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.33677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anderson acceleration (AA) can markedly reduce iteration counts for fixed-point solvers, but its unrestricted signed history extrapolation need not preserve the stability required for iterative regularization of ill-posed problems. We introduce a regularization-guaranteed Anderson-accelerated Landweber method (\RG) in which finite-memory AA generates a proposal while the committed iterate is a controlled perturbation of a certified Landweber anchor. Under a local tangential cone condition and a scale-normalized localization condition, we prove strong convergence of the exact-data trajectory to a solution, stability at every fixed iteration, finite discrepancy stopping, and strong convergence of the discrepancy-stopped noisy reconstructions to the same exact-data limit; local uniqueness is needed only if that selected limit is to be identified with a prescribed solution $x^\dagger$. Under the additional benchmark source condition $x^\dagger-x_0=F'(x^\dagger)^*\lambda^\dagger$ and a standard range-invariance condition, we obtain the discrepancy-principle rate $\norm{x_{k_\delta}^\delta-x^\dagger}=O(\delta^{1/2})$. The rate proof controls data-dependent Anderson coefficients through fixed memory, a fixed-reference ridge in the small AA least-squares problem, and an outer correction budget with an $O(k^{-1})$ tail. The numerical examples verify the efficiency of the proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Jianming Gao, Xiliang Lu, Lin Tian

item.title: A fast tangential rational Krylov subspace method with randomized sketching for large Lyapunov matrix equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.33684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a tangential rational Krylov subspace method augmented with randomized sketching for solving continuous-time Lyapunov equations $AX + XA^T + BB^T = 0$, where $A$ is large and sparse and $B$ has a rank much higher than one. Numerical solutions require high-dimensional rational Krylov subspaces (e.g., of dimensions up to $\sim 1000$), leading to substantial computational cost and long runtime. Building on the adaptive strategies of [SIAM\,J.\,Matrix\,Anal.\,Appl., 35\,(2014), pp.\,476--498], which expand the subspace using the most relevant directions, we introduce several enhancements: selective orthogonalization of basis vectors and fast residual-norm estimation enabled by randomized sketching, and the option to use either adaptive distinct poles or a small set of repeated poles. We derive a new computable error bound for the approximate solutions and show that sketching does not degrade the convergence rate relative to the standard (non-sketched) algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved robustness and efficiency, with reduced runtimes and often higher accuracy than the standard tangential method.
item.dc:creator: Tianqi Zhang, Fei Xue

item.title: Two 3-Dimensional Coefficient Inverse Problems for Wave-like Equations With a Single Location of the Point Source
item.description: arXiv:2611.33688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper two long standing open questions are addressed for the first time. Those questions are about Lipschitz stability estimates and uniqueness theorems for two Coefficient Inverse Problems (CIPs) for 3-Dimensional wave-like Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) with formally determined input data. We assume that a certain associated PDE is written in finite differences with respect to time t. The unknown coefficients depend on all three spatial variables. The key novelty here is that the input data for these CIPs are generated by only a single location of the point source at the moment of time {t = 0}. In the first CIP (CIP1) the unknown coefficient is the potential of a wave-like PDE. The second CIP (CIP2) is concerned with a far more challenging case when the unknown coefficient is involved in the principal part of the hyperbolic operator. In addition to Lipschitz stability and uniqueness results, numerical methods are developed for both CIPs. Their convergence analysis establishes the global convergence property of both numerical techniques. The latter is unlike the local convergence of conventional numerical procedures for CIPs. The method for CIP1 is tested computationally. Its extensive numerical testing for complicated media structures consistently demonstrates a very accurate performance of this method for noisy input data. The authors declare that artificial intelligence was not used for any part of this work.
item.dc:creator: Michael V. Klibanov, Jingzhi Li, Tian Niu

item.title: A Nonlocal Allen--Cahn Model for Volume-Constrained Wetting and Its Multi-Structure-Preserving Discretization
item.description: arXiv:2611.33754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At finite interface thickness, small droplets can shrink or disappear during wetting relaxation even when the phase-field mass is conserved. We develop a nonlocal Allen--Cahn model that couples a nonlinear diffuse-volume constraint to dynamic wall relaxation through Onsager's principle. The constraint gradient vanishes at the pure-phase values and does zero work in the energy balance, preserving the original bulk and wall dissipation structure. We construct a Compatible Variational Chain-Rule (CVC) scheme using the same discrete derivative of the volume density in the correction and in the volume increment. The scheme exactly conserves the nonlinear diffuse volume and reproduces the bulk--wall dissipation identity for the original discrete energy. Under a coercivity condition, the energy also yields a mesh-dependent maximum-norm bound. Numerical tests show second-order convergence in space and time. In flat-wall tests, the proposed model improves small-droplet retention and geometric-volume preservation and reproduces equilibrium cap shapes and contact angles. Additional tests illustrate wetting on chemically heterogeneous and rough substrates.
item.dc:creator: Yadong Liu, Nan Lu, Zhonghua Qiao, Yuze Zhang

item.title: Structure Preserving Iterative Solution of Linear Systems Arising in Gauss Collocation for port-Hamiltonian DAEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.33969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents structure-preserving computational techniques for the pencil Pad\'e approximation arising in the numerical integration of port-Hamiltonian differential-algebraic equations (pH-DAEs) via the Gauss-Legendre schemes. We first extend the concept of the diagonal Pad\'e approximation and introduce a generalized framework characterizing the $s$-stage Gauss method. We further examine its structural properties and the role of the full orthogonalization method (FOM) in approximating the discrete solution. Building on this, we analyze the iterative approximation of the pencil Pade approximation and establish conditions on the search space in Petrov-Galerkin-type approximations which guarantee that structure-induced properties, such as dissipativity or energy preservation, are inherited by the Petrov-Galerkin approximations. In particular, we show that FOM-based Krylov subspace methods preserve these properties iterate-wise. The presented results provide a new insight into the interplay between Krylov subspace methods and energy preservation in the numerical integration of pH-DAEs. Finally, we conclude with numerical examples illustrating the convergence and the conservation of the physical properties.
item.dc:creator: Malak Diab, Andreas Frommer, Karsten Kahl, Stefan Maier, Nicole Marheineke

item.title: Model and higher-order structure-preserving scheme for the chemotaxis equations modeling the growth of bacterial colonies
item.description: arXiv:2611.34023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the model and higher-order structure-preserving numerical scheme for the chemotaxis equations modeling the growth of bacterial colonies. By using a new variational analysis method, we first rigidly derive the nonnegativity for two solutions of the chemotaxis equations. Then, utilizing the finite element method with mass-lumping in space and the BDF scheme with the positivity-preserving extrapolation to deal with the nonlinear terms in time, we propose a high-order fully discrete framework for the chemotaxis equations by combining with the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) shift and the Lagrange multiplier method, which preserves the mass conservation of the discrete system and the nonnegativity of two approximation solutions. Moreover, apart from confirming the existence and uniqueness of the nonlinear equation generated by the Lagrange multiplier method, by classifying its structure in detail, we prove that the secant iteration method for this nonlinear equation is locally convergent. Finally, we show some experiments to verify the theoretical prediction and efficiency of the proposed scheme, including consistent simulations of the growth of the colonies under different nutrient concentration and agar hardness.
item.dc:creator: Shuyan Ren, Kun Wang, Nianyu Yi

item.title: Conjugation-preserving polynomial and rational interpolation for limited-memory matrix-function actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.34028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Approximating $f(A)b$ for a large nonsymmetric matrix can require substantial storage if a long Krylov basis is retained. We develop polynomial and rational interpolation schemes that use a fixed number of large recurrence vectors and preserve conjugation symmetry. Starting from a prescribed scalar approximation region, the schemes organize real nodes and complex-conjugate pairs into Newton-like bases with real interpolation coefficients. The polynomial and single-real-pole recurrences use real arithmetic in the matrix-action stage; the multi-pole construction also exploits conjugate pole pairs. A conjugation-preserving AAA procedure supplies interpolation data for the latter. We establish the interpolation and basis properties and compare the resulting realizations with Leja, Taylor, and Krylov methods on matrices from differential equations, model reduction, and networks. The experiments demonstrate arithmetic savings relative to complex-arithmetic counterparts and identify the influence of shifted solves and orthogonalization requirements. The methods are intended for memory-constrained computations in which useful approximation-region information is available.
item.dc:creator: Tianqi Zhang, Fei Xue

item.title: Exact Integration of ReLU-type Neural Networks for Solving PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.34085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developing robust training methodologies for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with neural networks is crucial for reliable scientific computing. Piecewise-linear activations such as the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) are a convenient choice in this setting as their structure resembles classical piecewise-linear approximations. However, when the loss functional incorporates the spatial gradient of the network, as in the Deep Ritz method, numerical integration becomes problematic. Specifically, relying on standard integration techniques (e.g., Monte Carlo sampling) during training yields incorrect gradients, even as the number of integration points approaches infinity, leading to optimization failure. To overcome this limitation, we present an integration framework for single-hidden-layer ReLU networks that computes correct gradients when using Deep Ritz for PDEs or PINNs for first-order problems. Our approach employs the Sutherland-Hodgman algorithm to partition the physical domain into subdomains according to breaking hyperplanes underlying the ReLU network. By finding these hyperplanes exactly, our method can correctly integrate the gradients, ensuring the optimizer receives correct information. In this work, we further assemble the energy in matrix--vector form that allows all neuron interactions to be computed efficiently with vectorized operations, introduce an alternative approach termed Conforming Monte Carlo that is a stochastic version of the proposed method, and propose two stochastic training strategies to reduce complexity. Numerical results on two-dimensional domains demonstrate that our framework recovers optimal PDE solutions that standard stochastic sampling and other existing quadrature methods fail to capture.
item.dc:creator: Shima Baharlouei, Ignacio Brevis, Reuben Menezes, David Pardo, Kristoffer G. van der Zee

item.title: Simultaneous Inversion of Drift and Potential in the Fractional Magnetic Schr\"odinger Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.34189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Calder\'on problem for the fractional magnetic Schr\"odinger equation with drift in the bivariate additive framework. When the magnetic potential $A$ is known and fixed, we prove that the drift $b$ and the scalar potential $q$ can be simultaneously and uniquely determined from exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann measurements. When $A$ is unknown, we prove that the triple $(A,b,q)$ can only be recovered up to a natural gauge equivalence class, and that the drift $b$ is a gauge invariant, hence uniquely determined. The proofs rely on the Alessandrini identity, Runge approximation, and the unique continuation property for fractional magnetic operators. Furthermore, we have developed a numerical reconstruction framework that combines finite difference discretization, radial basis function surrogate modeling, and smoothed TV regularization. One-dimensional and two-dimensional numerical examples have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method and supported the theoretical uniqueness result.
item.dc:creator: Yun-Long Liu, Jin Wen, Jun-Liang Fu, Xue-Juan Ren

item.title: Sharp Query Bounds and Optimal Faithful Simulation under Smooth Changes of Variables
item.description: arXiv:2611.33189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider deterministic procedures that acquire information about an unknown real-valued function through scalar queries to its values and derivatives. We use two descriptions of computation, one in terms of states and transitions and another in terms of rules depending on the history of responses, allowing partially defined rules. We establish representations in both directions that exactly preserve the domains of valid computations within a finite budget, their outputs, records, and counts by derivative order. These representations make it possible to study the cost of reproducing derivative information under changes of variables. For a composite function $f\circ\chi$, with $\chi$ a known smooth diffeomorphism, we prove that the minimum number of queries to $f$ needed to reconstruct a derivative response equals the number of nonzero coefficients in the composition formula, even among adaptive procedures. We extend this characterization to faithful simulation of complete procedures and obtain the exact cost from the union of the active data in their records. For successive changes of variables, we determine the costs of reconstructing intermediate responses and of computing only the final derivative, and characterize the savings due to cancellation of data. Finally, upon composing a smooth change with its inverse, we prove that the direct cost is one, whereas the intermediate reconstruction cost remains equal to one if all higher derivatives of the change vanish at the point and tends to infinity with the order otherwise. In particular, affine changes are exactly those that admit a uniform bound on this cost over all points and orders.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Alberto Castro Mar\'in

item.title: CAMPS: Composable Adapters for Mixed-Precision Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2611.33703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mixed-precision solvers usually assign a fixed precision to each algorithmic component. This makes it hard to reuse a lower-precision solver at different depths inside a higher-precision solver. We introduce CAMPS (Composable Adapters for Mixed-Precision Solvers), a framework that uses iterative refinement to connect solvers across precisions. An adapter computes residuals and updates in the precision of its parent and passes each correction solve to a child solver in a lower precision. The child can be a direct solver, an iterative solver, or another adapter. The adapter checks every correction and keeps it if the residual does not increase. We prove three results. Adapters can be placed at any compatible set of precision boundaries in a solver tree without breaking the solver interface. Every output that the root solver reports as successful satisfies a backward-error bound set by the stopping tolerance and the root precision. Convergence follows from one sufficient condition per boundary, computed from the leaves of the tree to its root. We test five configurations on dense and sparse systems in 64-bit, 32-bit, and 16-bit floating-point arithmetic (FP64, FP32, and FP16). On dense well-conditioned systems, CAMPS is up to 9.6x faster than an FP64 direct solver for a single solve that includes the factorization. On sparse nonsymmetric systems, a three-precision hierarchy is the fastest method we tested. Compared with our implementation of the nested solver F3R, CAMPS is as fast and uses about 3.4x less peak memory. CAMPS does not always win. Plain conjugate gradient is faster on sparse symmetric positive definite systems. On very ill-conditioned systems, FP32 corrections fail, and the adapter detects the failure and switches to an FP64 fallback.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Li, Chandrajit Bajaj

item.title: A nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme II: multi-frequency radiation transport
item.description: arXiv:2611.33718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conventional discrete ordinate methods are widely used for thermal radiative transfer, but their fixed number of angular degrees of freedom (DoFs) incurs unnecessary computational cost near equilibrium. We therefore develop a nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme (NCUGKS) for multi-frequency radiation transport. The scheme preserves the mul tiscale capability of UGKS through interface evolution that couples transport and collision. Radiation intensity is expanded in an orthonormal basis of the discrete angular space. The expansion coefficients serve as angular DoFs, with their number adapted independently to local nonequilibrium in each cell, frequency group, and quadrant. At each time step, the coefficients to be evolved are selected using the exponentially decayed contribution from the previous step and the requirements of interface transport. The selected coefficients are advanced by the finite volume scheme and corrected to match the macroscopic radiation energy before higher-degree coefficients are discarded according to the prescribed relative tail tolerance. Therefore, in the optically thick limit, the resulting representation retains only one angular DoF per quadrant. Numerical tests spanning different optical regimes show close agreement with reference solutions, validating its accuracy. Furthermore, in terms of memory and computational efficiency, the proposed method reduces memory by factors from 21.7 to 154.0 and achieves speedups from 24.87 to 257.9 compared with the original discrete ordinate UGKS. NCUGKS thus provides the ability to accurately simulate multiscale ra diative transfer with reduced memory and computational costs. The proposed approach also offers a framework for adapting angular degrees of freedom in other discrete ordinate methods.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Liu, Xiaojian Yang, Xing Ji, Jianxian Qiu, Kun Xu

item.title: Data-driven framework for invariant manifold identification in multiscale systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.33849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multiscale dynamical systems often exhibit fast transient behavior followed by slow evolution on a low-dimensional attracting manifold, on which their long-term dynamics unfold. Identifying this structure directly from data remains challenging when the governing equations, Jacobians, and fast-slow variable partitions are unknown. In this work, we propose a fully data-driven framework for timescale decomposition, slow invariant manifold (SIM) approximation, and reduced-order model identification. A sparse-regression surrogate of the vector field is reconstructed from the data, and its Jacobian, estimated with a matrix-free Krylov method, is analysed with Computational Singular Perturbation diagnostics. The resulting fast-slow partition guides the learning of explicit SIM algebraic representations through regression, and the reduced model follows by restricting the dynamics to it. For a linear stochastic system, this regression agrees with the Mori-Zwanzig projection at leading order in the timescale ratio. We demonstrate the validity of the framework on an illustrative linear system, the Michaelis-Menten model, a biofilm growth model, and a five-dimensional target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) model. The method accurately identifies fast variables, reconstructs slow invariant manifolds, and generates accurate reduced models. Furthermore, we map the performance boundaries of the framework under sparse sampling and measurement noise, showing robust recovery for low-dimensional systems and highlighting data-requirement limits in higher dimensions. These results demonstrate that interpretable multiscale reduction can be achieved directly from time-series data, without requiring explicit prior knowledge of the underlying fast/slow timescale separation.
item.dc:creator: Dimitris M. Manias, Ismaila Muhammed, Dimitris A. Goussis, Haralampos Hatzikirou

item.title: Reduced Order Modeling of Partial Differential Equations on Parameter-Dependent Domains Using Deep Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2407.17171v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) are widely used for modeling various physical phenomena. These equations often depend on certain parameters, necessitating either the identification of optimal parameters or the solution of the equations over multiple parameters. Performing an exhaustive search over the parameter space requires solving the PDE multiple times, which is generally impractical. To address this challenge, reduced order models (ROMs) are built using a set of precomputed solutions (snapshots) corresponding to different parameter values. Recently, Deep Learning ROMs (DL-ROMs) have been introduced as a new method to obtain ROM, offering improved flexibility and performance. In many cases, the domain on which the PDE is defined also varies. Capturing this variation is important for building accurate ROMs but is often difficult, especially when the domain has a complex structure or changes topology. In this paper, we propose a Deep-ROM framework that can automatically extract useful domain parametrization and incorporate it into the model. Unlike traditional domain parameterization methods, our approach does not require user-defined control points and can effectively handle domains with varying numbers of components. It can also learn from domain data even when no mesh is available. Using deep autoencoders, our approach reduces the dimensionality of both the PDE solution and the domain representation, making it possible to approximate solutions efficiently across a wide range of domain shapes and parameter values. We demonstrate that our approach produces parametrizations that yield solution accuracy comparable to models using exact parameters. Importantly, our model remains stable under moderate geometric variations in the domain, such as boundary deformations and noise - scenarios where traditional ROMs often require remeshing or manual adjustment.
item.dc:creator: Martina Buka\v{c} (University of Notre Dame, Notre Dame, IN, USA), Iva Miku\v{s} (University of Zagreb Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing, Croatia), Boris Muha (Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Science, University of Zagreb, Croatia), Domagoj Vlah (University of Zagreb Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing, Croatia)

item.title: Learned Finite Element-based Regularization of the Inverse Problem in Electrocardiographic Imaging
item.description: arXiv:2602.07466v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electrocardiographic imaging (ECGI) seeks to reconstruct cardiac electrical activity from body-surface potentials noninvasively. However, the associated inverse problem is severely ill-posed and requires robust regularization. While classical approaches primarily employ spatial smoothing, the temporal structure of cardiac dynamics remains underexploited despite its physiological relevance. We introduce a space-time regularization framework that couples spatial regularization with a learned temporal Fields-of-Experts (FoE) prior to capture complex spatiotemporal activation patterns. We derive a finite element discretization on unstructured cardiac surface meshes, prove Mosco-convergence, and develop a scalable optimization algorithm capable of handling the FoE term. Numerical experiments on synthetic epicardial data demonstrate improved denoising and inverse reconstructions compared to handcrafted spatiotemporal methods, yielding solutions that are both robust to noise and physiologically plausible.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Haas, Thomas Grandits, Thomas Pinetz, Thomas Beiert, Simone Pezzuto, Alexander Effland

item.title: Computing and Optimizing the $H^2$-norm of Delay Differential Algebraic Systems
item.description: arXiv:2603.10734v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a Lanczos tau method for the approximation and optimization of the $H^2$-norm of time-delay systems described by delay differential algebraic equations of index one. The soundness of this approach is proven under the assumption of a finite strong $H^2$-norm. Furthermore, we prove convergence if the rational approximation of the exponential underlying the discretization is well-behaved and the discretization is stability preserving. Numerical results suggest that, for multiple delays, the method converges at cubic rate in the discretization degree for systems of retarded type and linearly for those of neutral type. In the single delay case, we note geometric convergence of the $H^2$-norm for systems of both retarded and neutral type when a symmetric basis is chosen. Explicit formulas are derived for the gradient of the approximation with respect to system parameters and delays. These allow us to compute the entire gradient using only about double the computational time of approximating the $H^2$-norm alone. We illustrate how these can be used to synthesize robust feedback controllers and stable approximate models. The article is concluded by a discussion of how the presented results extend and improve for approximations based on splines. We note acceleration of the convergence rate by a little over a full order for such a choice. Finally, we prove that a Lanczos tau method using a spline based on Legendre orthogonal polynomials preserves stability and guarantees convergence of the $H^2$-norm.
item.dc:creator: Evert Provoost, Wim Michiels

item.title: A High-Order Fast Direct Solver for Surface PDEs on Triangles
item.description: arXiv:2604.03097v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop a triangular formulation of the hierarchical Poincar\'e--Steklov (HPS) method for elliptic partial differential equations on surfaces. It admits high-order discretizations on unstructured triangular meshes of complex geometries, with spectral collocation in the orthogonal Dubiner basis on each element. As in quadrilateral HPS, local solution operators and Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps are built and merged hierarchically, yielding a fast direct solver with $\mathcal O(N \log N)$ complexity for repeated solves on meshes with $N$ elements. Since the precomputed operators are reused for every elliptic solve, the solver also accelerates high-order implicit time-stepping schemes on surfaces. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order convergence under mesh refinement and spectral accuracy under polynomial refinement for static and time-dependent test problems.
item.dc:creator: Gentian Zavalani

item.title: Incremental SVD for Large-Scale Dynamic Matrices: Accuracy, Subspace Stability, Refresh Strategies, and Financial Factor-Based Risk Models
item.description: arXiv:2605.24514v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Return panels, covariances, and large feature matrices evolve one observation or entry at a time, yet downstream models require an up-to-date low-rank factorization $A_t \approx U_t \Sigma_t V_t^\top$ on every tick - a regime where a full singular value decomposition (SVD) is prohibitive and existing alternatives sacrifice singular vectors, singular values, or long-horizon stability. We present a metric-driven study of Brand-style incremental SVD, built around a unified engine that handles row appends, column appends, rank-1 entry updates, and metrics tracking. For rank-1 entry updates, we derive an explicit projection-based rule $U'\Sigma'(V')^\top = P_U(\widehat{A} + \delta\,e_ie_j^\top)P_V$ that keeps rank fixed while discarding only the out-of-subspace remainder quantifiably, turning Brand's rank-suppression heuristic into an operational scheme. Each update discards a part whose norm is available at negligible cost; the error at the last refresh plus the sum of these norms since then is an a posteriori error bound $\beta_t$. We then treat refresh scheduling as a first-class design axis, comparing periodic refresh with a bound-triggered rule that refreshes once $\beta_t/\|A_t\|_F$ exceeds a tolerance. The engine tracks error ratios, principal angles, explained variance, and per-update runtime on long synthetic streams and a factor model of exchange-traded funds for covariance and portfolio-risk estimation. With a sensible rank and refresh cadence, incremental SVD matches full-SVD accuracy within a few percent at a fraction of the cost. The bound-triggered rule keeps the relative error below any tolerance above its rank-$k$ optimum, with accuracy close to periodic refresh at a matched number of full SVDs.
item.dc:creator: Stilyan Staykov

item.title: On the First Derivative Bounds for Rational B\'ezier Curves
item.description: arXiv:2607.10425v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive a new upper bound for the first derivative of a rational B\'ezier curve of degree $n$. The estimate applies to arbitrary degrees and provides a framework for studying the linear bound conjectured by Li et al., whose coefficient is the maximal adjacent weight ratio $\Omega$. Within this framework, the conjectured bounds for $n=5$ and $n=6$ are established as special cases, completing the verification for all $n\le6$. The endpoint estimates follow from the classical derivative formulas. For interior parameters, the analysis reduces to a variance-like optimization problem over a compact box of adjacent weight ratios. A block argument reduces the maximization to vertices and one-dimensional faces, leading to a finite family of polynomial inequalities. We further prove that sufficiently fine subdivision yields subcurves satisfying the conjectured estimate with their own weights, control points and local parameters. After parameter rescaling, these local estimates provide a bound for the derivative of the original curve. Numerical examples illustrate the new bound and the subdivision-based estimates and compare them with an existing method.
item.dc:creator: Mao Shi

item.title: Near-Optimal Learning of Gaussian Sobolev Operators
item.description: arXiv:2607.11921v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A key question in operator learning is how to design surrogate operators with provable approximation guarantees in reasonable computational time. Whereas holomorphic operators can be approximated efficiently, i.e., with at least algebraic convergence in the number of training samples, learning finitely regular operators is known to be less efficient. The reason is an intrinsic curse of sample complexity, which allows only subalgebraic convergence rates. This fact makes it all the more important to develop algorithms which provably achieve these rates. In this work, we present a fully data-driven algorithm, termed Hermite-PCA approximation, for learning Gaussian Sobolev operators with near-optimal sample complexity. It employs principal component analysis and weighted least-squares methods and is therefore computationally efficient. Moreover, it is spectral, in the sense that it achieves faster (and near-optimal) convergence as the Sobolev regularity increases. We provide a full error analysis of this algorithm along with numerical experiments that match our theoretical results and empirically confirm the efficacy of Hermite-PCA approximation for learning Sobolev operators.
item.dc:creator: Ben Adcock, Michael Griebel, Gregor Maier

item.title: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification
item.description: arXiv:2607.15832v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Can a model be identified from one experiment? We study analytic systems that are linearly parameterized by a combination of prescribed dictionary terms, such as partial differential operators and dynamical systems. For a single input-response pair, recovery is possible exactly when the evaluated dictionary terms are linearly independent. We prove a sharp zero-one law: either no input uniquely determines the coefficients, or almost every random input sampled from a nondegenerate Gaussian measure does. This dichotomy reduces one-shot system identification to a question about degenerate inputs and provides an a posteriori certificate in the noiseless setting. Numerical examples recover dynamical systems, nonlinear partial differential equations, and structured matrix families from single trajectory data, while also detecting when an extra probe is necessary.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Boull\'e, Diana Halikias, Samuel E. Otto, Alex Townsend

item.title: Convergence of entropy-conservative summation-by-parts discretizations to smooth solutions of hyperbolic conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2607.27049v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Although entropy-based summation-by-parts (SBP) discretizations of hyperbolic conservation laws are widely used for their robustness and stability properties, there are very few results on their convergence. We extend a recent convergence analysis of Worku, Del Rey Fern\'andez, and Zingg (2026, DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2603.18369) in two ways. First, instead of allowing only hyperbolic conservation laws whose fluxes are homogeneous and have globally bounded second derivatives (a restriction essentially to linear or quadratic fluxes), we consider general hyperbolic systems with strictly convex entropy and source terms depending on time and space. Second, instead of requiring a special class of SBP operators, we consider a general framework of diagonal-norm SBP operators on curved meshes, including finite differences, continuous and discontinuous Galerkin methods. Since the error analysis is based on a discrete relative entropy, it is restricted to smooth solutions. To enable a unified treatment of conservation laws, we restrict the analysis to periodic boundary conditions. Numerical results demonstrate that the predicted convergence rates are sharp in general, but can be improved for special cases such as discontinuous Galerkin methods with even polynomial degree and multi-block finite difference methods. An optimal analysis is expected to require more sophisticated arguments specialized to the class of methods instead of the general framework of SBP operators used in this work.
item.dc:creator: Hendrik Ranocha

item.title: Nearly sharp $W^{1,\infty}$ stability of polynomial spectral Ritz projections
item.description: arXiv:2610.19531v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the first time, we establish nearly sharp $W^{1,\infty}$ stability estimates for the Legendre spectral Ritz projection associated with the Laplacian on a square domain. The $W^{1,\infty}$ operator norm of this projection is of order $N^{1/2}$, up to logarithmic factors, where $N$ is the polynomial degree. The upper bound uses a resolvent representation of the discrete gradient projection and a rank-two comparison controlled by terminal-column energy estimates. The lower bound follows from an explicit zero-trace polynomial whose Ritz projection is computed exactly. As an application, we derive sharp maximum-norm error estimates for the Poisson and heat equations.
item.dc:creator: Yongxing Guo, Yuwen Li

item.title: Numerical simulations of CCP-2D GEC with sGMRES
item.description: arXiv:2611.30211v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fluid models provide an efficient means of simulating the low-temperature gas discharges, which are important in semiconductor manufacturing. This work presents, to the best of our knowledge, the first systematic numerical framework for the Gaseous Electronics Conference (GEC) reference cell of the 2D capacitively coupled plasma (CCP). The framework employs a structured, nonuniform cylindrical mesh to resolve the spatial gradients. A semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is used for the Poisson's equation, while the implicit SG schemes are applied to the continuity equations and the electron energy equation. Both the explicit and and the implicit formulations based on the conventional drift-diffusion terms are also investigated. To solve the resulting large-scale linear systems, we introduce an incomplete LU (ILU)-preconditioned sketched GMRES (sGMRES) method as the solver. As far as we know, this work is the first to apply the randomized sGMRES to the practical simulations in the engineering. By reducing the cost of the global orthogonalization, ILU-sGMRES achieves greater computational efficiency than ILU-GMRES while maintaining the accuracy, particularly at relatively large values of the restart. Specifically, numerical tests demonstrate that ILU-sGMRES can reduce the end-to-end wall-clock time by up to 25.38\% on a single machine and up to 11.71\% in a three-node benchmark compared with the conventional ILU-GMRES, while maintaining a maximum relative difference across plasma fields of only 0.194\%. Numerical experiments compare the performance of different numerical schemes and solvers, demonstrating the robustness of ILU-sGMRES in the real simulation.
item.dc:creator: Zhenyu Zou, Haoran Guan, Kangxin Liu, Yufeng Wei, Yipei Chen, Peiting You, Yuwei Fan

item.title: Relaxed magnetohydrodynamics with cross-field flow
item.description: arXiv:2604.03545v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The phase-space Lagrangian model of Dewar et al. (Phys. Plasmas 27, 062507, 2020) provides a framework for incorporating cross-field flow into relaxed equilibria while retaining ideal magnetohydrodynamics force balance. Here, we characterize the steady-state solution space and identify a solvability condition that couples the prescribed constrained flow to the geometry through the metric tensor. Using this condition, we construct equilibria in slab, cylindrical, and toroidal geometries. In toroidal geometry, the cross-field flow strongly correlates with magnetic-island structure: varying the rotation frequency modifies the dominant Fourier harmonic of the radial component of the magnetic field and can drive a transition from a primary (m = 1) island to secondary (m = 2) islands. In slab and cylindrical geometries, flow parameters weakly affect island width but strongly modify equilibrium profiles.
item.dc:creator: Arash Tavassoli, Stuart R. Hudson, Zhisong Qu, Matthew Hole

item.title: An Implicit Compact-Kernel Material Point Method for Computational Solid Mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2604.18917v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The numerical performance of the material point method (MPM) is strongly governed by the particle-grid kernel, which controls the trade-off among smoothness, locality, numerical diffusion, contact accuracy, and computational cost. Although wide-support smooth kernels can effectively suppress cell-crossing instability, they often introduce increased numerical diffusion, artificial contact gaps, and higher transfer cost. In contrast, the suitability of compact-kernel designs for implicit computational solid mechanics remains unclear. In this work, we develop an implicit formulation of the Compact-Kernel Material Point Method (CK-MPM) building on the framework of Liu et al. [2025], and assess its performance through benchmark problems in linear and nonlinear solid mechanics. Numerical assessment comprises cantilever bending, Hertzian contact, narrow-clearance free fall, and colliding hyperelastic rings, supplemented by a transfer-only diffusion test and spatial and temporal refinement studies. Implicit CK-MPM mitigates the cell-crossing stress noise and numerical energy loss observed in linear MPM, while retaining bending and energy responses comparable to those of quadratic B-spline MPM. Meanwhile, its more localized transfers improve contact-pressure accuracy and reduce the artificial contact gaps and early-contact artifacts associated with the wider-support quadratic kernel. These results demonstrate that the developed implicit formulation retains CK-MPM's favorable balance between smoothness and transfer locality in static and dynamic solid-mechanics analysis.
item.dc:creator: Qirui Fu, Yupeng Jiang, Minchen Li

item.title: Adaptive Volumetric Parameterization of Simply Connected 3-Manifolds with Applications
item.description: arXiv:2608.08672v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Volumetric parameterization, the process of mapping a 3-manifold onto a simplified volumetric domain, is important for many tasks in computer graphics and imaging science. However, most prior volumetric parameterization approaches have only utilized standardized domains such as a solid ball regardless of the overall shape of the given 3-manifolds, which introduces significant geometric distortion and affects the subsequent shape processing and analysis tasks. To overcome this issue, in this work we propose a novel volumetric parameterization framework for simply connected 3-manifolds. Specifically, the proposed framework jointly controls local shape and mass distortions, while adapting the target domain during the optimization process. It enables three progressively more flexible target-domain settings for the parameterization: a prescribed solid ellipsoid, a volume-normalized adaptive ellipsoid with variable radii, and a sea-embedded free-boundary domain. For each setting, the parameterization algorithm consists of a 3D quasi-conformality shape update, a diffusion-based density-equalizing update, and a geometric correction procedure for removing element foldings, thereby allowing for volumetric parameterizations with different desired effects. Experimental results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework. Moreover, our framework can be easily applied to multiresolution and localized adaptive volumetric remeshing, volumetric registration, and volumetric morphing. Altogether, our work provides a new way for the representation, processing, and analysis of 3-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyuan Lyu, Qiguang Chen, Lok Ming Lui, Gary P. T. Choi

item.title: Karhunen-Lo\`eve Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11624v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Karhunen-Lo\`eve transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix, below 1.2 percent for the $8\times8$ Markov block at pole $0.95$. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra. A moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exactly for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows. The dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means. This version adds complex data on the cyclic group with a border departure of rank exactly $2p$, the mixed and integrated classes, odd-length cores, and a released implementation whose kernel evaluation counts are flat in $M\log_2(M/n_{\mathrm{leaf}})$ to 5.3 percent. Experiments on recorded acoustic-array, radar and vibration data state where the transform helps and where existing methods match it.
item.dc:creator: Mitchell A. Thornton

item.title: Self-adjoint boundary conditions for equation-free multiscale modelling
item.description: arXiv:2611.18788v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Equation-free modelling is a computation multiscale modelling scheme for the simulation of complex dynamical systems. Efficient computations are achieved by solving the given microscale model in small, well-separated `patches' spread across the space-time domain, with each patch providing a data point for the macroscale simulation. Patch coupling bridges the unsimulated space between patches and supports the macroscale dynamics. Accurate simulations require coupling conditions that preserve underlying symmetries of the microscale equation. Failing to preserve such symmetries may result in an unphysical macroscale simulation that does not satisfy required conservation laws. Here we develop equation-free modelling that preserves self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models defined by a compact self-adjoint operator on a bounded domain with fixed boundary conditions. This new design for equation-free modelling greatly increases the range of systems for which equation-free modelling is applicable.
item.dc:creator: J. E. Bunder

item.title: On the computation of Green's function in layered elastic media
item.description: arXiv:2611.31852v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a recursive scheme for the computation of Green's function for time-harmonic elastic wave in three-dimensional layered media, based on a matrix basis representation in the Fourier domain and a classic interface reaction-transmission theory. With transversal rotational symmetry preserved, the scheme decouples the Green's function into SH waves and P-SV waves using five scalar functions, which are recursively solved at linear cost with respect to the number of total layers, regardless of the layers the source and target particles locate in. The resulting scheme leads to a stable numerical method ready for Hankel transform evaluation in the spatial domain, constituting a foundation for the analysis and efficient numerical simulation of elastic wave scattering in layered media.
item.dc:creator: Heng Yuan, Wenzhong Zhang, Bo Wang, Wei Cai
